solution:
Let \(\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}, \vec{b}=-3\hat{i}+4\hat{k}, \vec{c}=-\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k}, \vec{d}=-5\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) be the position vectors of A, B, C, D respectively.

\(\overline{AB} = \vec{b}-\vec{a} = -5\hat{i}+\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\)

\(\overline{AC} = \vec{c}-\vec{a} = -3\hat{i}+4\hat{k}\)

\(\overline{AD} = \vec{d}-\vec{a} = -2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\)

Consider: \(\overline{AB}\cdot(\overline{AC}\times\overline{AD}) = \begin{vmatrix} -5 & 1 & 4 \\ -3 & 0 & 4 \\ -2 & -4 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\)

\(= -5(0+16) - 1(-6+8) + 4(12)\)

\(= -80 - 2 + 48 = -34 \neq 0\)

Therefore, the points A, B, C, D are non-coplanar.
note: the determinant -5(16) - 1(2) + 4(12) = -80 - 2 + 48 is -34, not 34; still non-zero, so the conclusion (non-coplanar) stands.
